title: Model families
description: Which model-release name patterns bridge to which tier-level product slug (e.g. `grok-*` -> `grok`). This file is identity evidence for the resolution layer, not a scoring declaration: it names a bridge from a version-specific release name to the tier-level slug the vendor sells, so a run that discovers a new `grok-5` release can be pointed at the existing `grok` product rather than proposed as a new one. Every `pattern` -> `product` bridge is a human ruling recorded once, in `decided_in`, and applied everywhere. See docs/reference/identity.md.

version.description: Schema version. Bump only on a breaking shape change.

pattern.description: A lowercase glob over release names, e.g. `grok-*`: the tier-level slug plus a mandatory `-` separator and a trailing `*`. Matches any release name that starts with the given prefix. build/validate.py additionally requires the prefix (the pattern minus its trailing `-*`) to equal `product` exactly, so a family can never bridge to a product its own pattern does not name. When two families' prefixes overlap (`deepseek-*` / `deepseek-coder-*`), the longest matching pattern wins -- see docs/reference/identity.md.

product.description: The tier-level product slug this pattern bridges to. Must resolve to a real sources/products/<slug>.yaml.

decided_in.description: The pull request (or other record) that ruled this bridge, e.g. `#476`.

note.description: Why this pattern bridges to this product. Factual, not a restatement of the pattern.
